notes: Hard (14/30). Single-stage but the reasoning is dense: recover a directed DAG from observational samples by implementing an exactly specified greedy max-|Pearson-r| spanning tree (Prim from the first network column), orient every edge away from the unique declared root, and resolve ambiguous directions with a documented tie hierarchy (child preference, then the analogical child rule: partial correlation of the child with each tied candidate parent given the other, with a defined fallback when the partial correlation is undefined). Hidden cases include a dataset with two machine-exact |r| ties (a duplicated column) where resolving the tie in the wrong order yields a different directed edge set, a near-tie just outside the 1e-9 tolerance where over-applying the tolerance yields a wrong set, a non-first root, and negative-correlation edges. The verifier re-executes /app/solver.py on every hidden case and requires the directed edge set to match exactly and OLS slopes within 2e-6, so a misresolved ambiguity or a missing edge breaks set equality. Rubric weights reasoning_depth/debugging_ambiguity/hidden_case_generalization at 3; no tool breadth, dependency chain, or environment pressure.
